title: MARS-Seq
scope: Jaitin 2014 MARS-Seq implementation, including supported indexing and amplification organization. The extraction covers the assigned MARS-Seq strip and matching MARS-Seq poster rows. Per-cell well context and pooling are included from matching text. The omitted RNA-production/DNase interface and cell-index carrier across pooling remain blocking evidence gaps; molecular, cellular and plate indexing are supported at method level, without unverified local insertion stages.

operations.label: Establish the RNA substrate across the depicted DNase I interface
operations.description: The diagram routes double-stranded cDNA through an arrow captioned DNaseI directly toward RNA fragmentation, without drawing RNA production. The matched Illumina prose reports transcription to RNA followed by DNA-template digestion, and the registered review identifies T7-enabled linear amplification. The supplied Jaitin main text refers to supplementary methods but does not contain that reaction sequence. This boundary therefore records an unresolved primary-verification interface rather than asserting that DNase makes RNA.
operations.information_effect: The diagram connects the upstream tagged cDNA preparation to RNA fragmentation, while secondary text describes an RNA amplification intermediate. The local amplification history and its indexing continuity are unresolved for the scoped 2014 implementation.

method_scopes.rationale: All eight operations lie on the sole MARS-Seq target route identified by the card, matching catalogue heading and both poster rows; adjacent methods and the right chemistry panel do not extend scope. Jaitin 2014 main text confirms MARS-Seq, pooled processing and molecular/cellular/plate tags, while the matched catalogue describes first RT, pooling before second-strand synthesis and RNA transcription before DNA-template removal. The registered primary supplies only a supplementary pointer for local chemistry. Its linked supplementary asset is absent from the read-only registry, so the omitted RNA-production/DNase interface and cell-tag carrier across content pooling remain blocking implementation questions. The PCR operation asserts only the depicted physical library production; its former all-tag preservation effect has been removed because the tag complement of the exact PCR input is not established. Final-library tag associations remain qualified method-level interpretations. Applicability to the named target is established; full resolution of its declared indexing/amplification scope awaits the specified registered primary evidence.

What physical cellular tag carrier is established before per-cell cDNA-containing well contents are mixed, and how does that cell identity remain recoverable in the pooled preparation? Also establish the plate-tag carrier and introduction stage, and which tags are already present in the post-ligation RT product before the depicted PCR block. Cell attribution across pooling is blocking for the declared indexing scope. Exact barcode bases, lengths and read-cycle settings are unnecessary. No new source can resolve these claims in this read-only registry attempt.

The Illumina card/catalogue claims that fragmentation eliminates strand-specific information, but the supplied Jaitin main text does not specify the read orientation and the schematic retains an asymmetric terminal-tag route.
